observations: Photo 0 shows a MacBook Pro with System Information open, displaying model identifier 'MacBookPro18,3', serial number 'F8DHH0002000FAM', and macOS version 15.7.3.
The System Information window shows 32 GB of RAM, 1 TB SSD, and a 16-inch display.
The battery information shows 70% maximum capacity and 48 cycles.
The keyboard is black with white lettering, and the trackpad is large and centered.
The laptop is on a glass table in a store with 'SCHOOLBOY GADGETS' branding on the wall.
Photos 1 and 2 show the same laptop from different angles, with the same screen content and background.
The seller claims it is a 16-inch MacBook Pro with M4 Max chip, but the System Information shows 'Apple M1 Max' as the chip.
The model identifier 'MacBookPro18,3' corresponds to the 2021 16-inch MacBook Pro with M1 Max chip, not the M4 Max.

claims.claim: 16-inch MacBook Pro with the M4 Max chip
claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows 'Apple M1 Max' under System Information > Hardware > Processor, and model identifier 'MacBookPro18,3', which is the 2021 model with M1 Max, not M4 Max.
This is a subjective claim; no performance benchmarks or usage context are shown.

risks.risk: The laptop may be a modified or repurposed unit, or the seller is misrepresenting the chip (M1 Max vs M4 Max).
risks.proof: A clear shot of the actual chip label inside the device, or a screenshot of the System Information showing the correct processor name.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a 2021 M1 Max model, not as an M4 Max, which would be significantly more valuable.

risks.risk: Battery health is at 70% and has 48 cycles, which may affect resale value and performance over time.
risks.proof: A video or photo showing the battery health under real-world usage, or a full battery cycle test.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a used laptop with degraded battery, which reduces value.

risks.risk: The device may have been tampered with or has hidden damage not visible in photos.
risks.proof: A full 360-degree video of the device, including the underside, ports, and hinges, with a close-up of the serial number and any service history.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a used device with potential hidden defects, which lowers value.

proof_requests: A clear photo or video of the actual chip inside the device, or a screenshot of the System Information showing the processor name.
A video showing the battery health under real-world usage or a full battery cycle test.
A 360-degree video of the device, including the underside, ports, and hinges.
response.reason: The item is identifiable as a 2021 16-inch MacBook Pro with M1 Max chip, based on the model identifier and processor name in photo 0. The seller's claim of M4 Max is contradicted by the evidence. The device is priced at its worst case as a used M1 Max model, with battery health at 70% and 48 cycles. Hidden risks include potential misrepresentation of the chip and hidden damage, which are priced in as lower value until proven otherwise.
